utility.notes: Dana Point is absent from SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (re-verified directly this session, consistent with the same finding for neighboring San Clemente). Independent search results confirm SDG&E service directly within Dana Point, and SDG&E's own description states it serves 'San Diego County and southern Orange County.'

value.name: San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E)
value.notes: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA), the only CCA operating in Orange County, directly re-verified this session via its own homepage's 'Celebrating our member communities' listing as serving exactly four member cities: Buena Park, Fullerton, Irvine, and Fountain Valley. Dana Point is not among them, so San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Center for Sustainable Energy (CSE), on behalf of SDG&E, under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered across SDG&E's entire distribution territory (via CSE), which includes Dana Point — same statewide tier already independently verified for other SDG&E-territory records this session.

value: Call the Inspection Request Line at (949) 248-3590 with the permit number, site address, inspection type, requested date, gate code (if applicable), and a callback phone number
Inspections must be scheduled by 4:00pm the prior business day to be scheduled for the next business day; inspections are normally performed 8:00am-4:00pm
A printed copy of all Symbium-approved documents must be on site for the field inspection
Confirm the inspection time window via the city's 'Daily Inspections' page by 8:00am the morning of the inspection, or call (949) 248-3564; cancellations must be made before 8:00am that same morning

value.notes: The City's own page states SB 379 established 'instantaneous plan review practices' and that qualifying contractors 'can apply for instantaneous plan review approval via Symbium's portal,' with permits 'issued without manual review or an in-person visit.'

value.program_or_pathway: Symbium instant permitting (SB 379) / standard eTRAKIT Permit Portal for non-qualifying projects
other_conditions: Contractor must hold an active A, B, C-10, or C-46 license
Residential solar energy system must be no larger than 38.4 kW AC nameplate rating
Projects not meeting Symbium criteria must submit electronically through the eTRAKIT Permit Portal
